title.zh: 卷三一 補列傳第二三 王昕 弟晞
title.en: Volume 31 Biographies 23: Wang Xin; Wang Xi
title.raw: 卷三一 補列傳第二三 王昕 弟晞 Volume 31 Biographies 23: Wang Xin; Wang Xi

sentences.zh: 王昕 弟晞

translations.literal: Wang Xin; younger brother Xi
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xin; Wang Xi

sentences.zh: 王昕，字元景，北海劇人。

translations.literal: Wang Xin, styled Yuanjing, was a man of Ju in Beihai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xin, styled Yuanjing, was a man of Ju in Beihai commandery.

sentences.zh: 六世祖猛，秦苻堅丞相，家於華山之鄜城。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Meng was chancellor under Fu Jian of Former Qin; the family settled at Fucheng in Huashan.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Meng had been chancellor under Fu Jian of Former Qin; the family settled at Fucheng in Huashan.

sentences.zh: 父雲，仕魏朝有名望。

translations.literal: His father Yun served the Wei court with repute.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yun served the Wei court with repute.

sentences.zh: 昕少篤學讀書，太尉汝南王悅辟騎兵參軍。

translations.literal: In youth Xin was devoted to learning and reading; Grand Marshal Prince of Runan Yue engaged him as cavalry staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Xin was devoted to learning and reading; Grand Marshal Prince of Runan Yue engaged him as cavalry staff officer.

sentences.zh: 舊事，王出射，武服持刀陪從，昕未嘗依行列。

translations.literal: By custom, when a prince went out shooting, attendants wore martial garb and carried blades in escort; Xin never took his place in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, when a prince went out shooting, attendants wore martial garb and carried blades in escort; Xin never took his place in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 悅好逸遊，或騁騎信宿，昕輒棄還。

translations.literal: Yue loved idle wandering and sometimes galloped away for nights at a time; Xin would each time abandon the outing and return.
translations.idiomatic: Yue loved idle wandering and sometimes galloped away for nights at a time; Xin would each time abandon the outing and return.

sentences.zh: 悅乃令騎馬在前，手為驅策。

translations.literal: Yue then had him ride in front and drove the horse with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: Yue then had him ride in front and drove the horse with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 昕舍轡高拱，任為所之。

translations.literal: Xin let go the reins and sat with hands folded high; he let Yue take him wherever.
translations.idiomatic: Xin let go the reins and sat with hands folded high, letting Yue take him wherever he would.

sentences.zh: 左右言其誕慢。

translations.literal: Those about said he was insolently slow.
translations.idiomatic: Those about him said he was insolently slow.

sentences.zh: 悅曰：「府望惟在此賢，不可責也。

translations.literal: Yue said: "The house's hope is in this worthy alone; he cannot be blamed.
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "The house's hope is in this worthy alone; he cannot be blamed.

sentences.zh: 」悅數散錢於地，令諸佐爭拾之，昕獨不拾。

translations.literal: " Yue often scattered cash on the ground and had his staff scramble for it; Xin alone did not pick any up.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue often scattered cash on the ground and had his staff scramble for it; Xin alone did not pick any up.

sentences.zh: 悅又散銀錢以目昕，昕乃取其一。

translations.literal: Yue scattered silver coins with his eye on Xin; Xin then took one.
translations.idiomatic: Yue scattered silver coins with his eye on Xin; Xin then took one.

sentences.zh: 悅與府僚飲酒，起自移床。

translations.literal: Yue drank with his household staff; he rose and moved the couch himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yue drank with his household staff; he rose and moved the couch himself.

sentences.zh: 人爭進手，昕獨執版卻立。

translations.literal: Others scrambled to lend a hand; Xin alone held his tablet and stepped back.
translations.idiomatic: Others scrambled to lend a hand; Xin alone held his tablet and stepped back.

sentences.zh: 悅於是作色曰：「我帝孫帝子帝弟帝叔，今為宴適，親起輿床。

translations.literal: Yue then darkened his face and said: "I am the emperor's grandson, son, brother, and uncle; today at a feast I rise to move the couch myself.
translations.idiomatic: Yue then darkened his face and said, "I am the emperor's grandson, son, brother, and uncle; today at a feast I rise to move the couch myself.

sentences.zh: 卿是何人，獨為偃蹇！

translations.literal: What sort of man are you, to stand alone in such arrogance!
translations.idiomatic: What sort of man are you, to stand alone in such arrogance!

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「元景位望微劣，不足使殿下式瞻儀形，安敢以親王僚宷，從廝養之役。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Yuanjing's rank and standing are slight and low, unworthy of having Your Highness bow and show your bearing; how dare I, a prince's staff officer, follow menial service like groom and stable hand.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Yuanjing's rank and standing are slight and low, unworthy of having Your Highness bow and show your bearing; how dare I, a prince's staff officer, follow menial service like groom and stable hand.

sentences.zh: 」悅謝焉。

translations.literal: " Yue apologized.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue apologized.

sentences.zh: 坐上皆引滿酣暢，昕先起，臥閑室，頻召不至。

translations.literal: All at the seat drank their fill in high spirits; Xin rose first and lay in an idle room; summoned repeatedly, he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: All at the seat drank their fill in high spirits; Xin rose first and lay in an idle room; summoned repeatedly, he did not come.

sentences.zh: 悅乃自詣呼之曰：「懷其才而忽府主，可謂仁乎？

translations.literal: Yue then came in person and called: "You cherish talent yet slight the house master—can that be called humane?
translations.idiomatic: Yue then came in person and called, "You cherish talent yet slight the house master—can that be called humane?

sentences.zh: 」昕曰：「商辛沈湎，其亡也忽諸，府主自忽，微僚敢任其咎。

translations.literal: " Xin said: "King Zhou of Shang sank in debauchery; his fall came in an instant. The house master slighted himself; may a petty officer bear the blame?
translations.idiomatic: " Xin said, "King Zhou of Shang sank in debauchery; his fall came in an instant. The house master slighted himself; may a petty officer bear the blame?

sentences.zh: 」悅大笑而去。

translations.literal: " Yue laughed loud and left.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue laughed loud and left.

sentences.zh: 累遷東萊太守。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to Administrator of Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to administrator of Donglai.

sentences.zh: 後吏部尚書李神儁奏言，比因多故，常侍遂無員限，今以王元景等為常侍，定限八員。

translations.literal: Later Minister of Personnel Li Shenjun memorialized saying that because of many disturbances the attendant-at-court posts had long had no fixed quota; now Wang Yuanjing and others were made attendants, fixed at eight.
translations.idiomatic: Later Minister of Personnel Li Shenjun memorialized that because of many disturbances the attendant-at-court posts had long had no fixed quota; now Wang Yuanjing and others were made attendants, fixed at eight.

sentences.zh: 加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the additional title grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 武帝或時袒露，與近臣戲狎，每見昕，即正冠而斂容焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Wei sometimes went bare-chested and sported familiarly with close ministers; whenever he saw Xin, he would straighten his cap and compose his bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Wei sometimes went bare-chested and sported familiarly with close ministers; whenever he saw Xin, he would straighten his cap and compose his bearing.

sentences.zh: 昕體素甚肥，遭喪後，遂終身羸瘠。

translations.literal: Xin's body had always been very stout; after mourning he remained gaunt for life.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's body had always been very stout; after mourning he remained gaunt for life.

sentences.zh: 楊愔重其德業，以為人之師表。

translations.literal: Yang Yin valued his virtue and learning and took him as a model for men.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin valued his virtue and learning and took him as a model for men.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書監。

translations.literal: He was moved to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 昕少與邢卲俱為元羅賓友，及守東萊，卲舉室就之。

translations.literal: In youth Xin and Xing Shao had both been guests of Yuan Luo; when Xin held Donglai, Shao brought his whole household to join him.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Xin and Xing Shao had both been guests of Yuan Luo; when Xin held Donglai, Shao brought his whole household to join him.

sentences.zh: 郡人以卲是邢杲從弟，會兵將執之，昕以身蔽伏其上，呼曰：「欲執邢子才，當先殺我。

translations.literal: The people of the commandery, because Shao was a cousin of Xing Gao, were mustering troops to seize him; Xin shielded him with his own body lying atop him and cried: "If you wish to seize Xing Zicai, you must kill me first.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the commandery, because Shao was a cousin of Xing Gao, were mustering troops to seize him; Xin shielded him with his own body lying atop him and cried, "If you wish to seize Xing Zicai, you must kill me first.

sentences.zh: 」卲乃免焉。

translations.literal: " Shao was thus spared.
translations.idiomatic: " Shao was thus spared.

sentences.zh: 昕雅好清言，詞無淺俗。

translations.literal: Xin was fond of pure talk; his words had nothing shallow or vulgar.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was fond of pure talk; his words had nothing shallow or vulgar.

sentences.zh: 在東萊，獲殺其同行侶者，詰之未服，昕謂之曰：「彼物故不歸，卿無恙而反，何以自明？

translations.literal: In Donglai he caught one who had killed a traveling companion; questioned, the man would not confess; Xin said to him: "That man died and did not return; you came back unharmed—how will you clear yourself?
translations.idiomatic: In Donglai he caught one who had killed a traveling companion; questioned, the man would not confess; Xin said to him, "That man died and did not return; you came back unharmed—how will you clear yourself?

sentences.zh: 」邢卲後見世宗，說此言以為笑樂。

translations.literal: " Later Xing Shao saw Gao Cheng and told this remark for a laugh.
translations.idiomatic: " Later Xing Shao saw Gao Cheng and told this remark for a laugh.

sentences.zh: 昕聞之，故詣卲曰：「卿不識造化。

translations.literal: When Xin heard of it, he went deliberately to Shao and said: "You do not understand creation.
translations.idiomatic: When Xin heard of it, he went deliberately to Shao and said, "You do not understand creation.

sentences.zh: 」還謂人曰：「子才應死，我罵之極深。」

translations.literal: " Returning, he told others: "Zicai ought to die; I cursed him to the utmost."
translations.idiomatic: " Returning, he told others, "Zicai ought to die; I cursed him to the utmost."

sentences.zh: 顯祖以昕疏誕，非濟世所須，罵之曰：「好門戶，惡人身。

translations.literal: Gao Yang, because Xin was loose and insolent and not what the age required, reviled him: "Fine house, vile person.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang, because Xin was loose and insolent and not what the age required, reviled him, "Fine house, vile person.

sentences.zh: 」又有讒之者曰：「王元景每嗟水運不應遂絕。

translations.literal: " There were also slanderers who said: "Wang Yuanjing often sighs that the water transport ought not to have been cut off.
translations.idiomatic: " There were also slanderers who said, "Wang Yuanjing often sighs that the water transport ought not to have been cut off.

sentences.zh: 」帝愈怒，乃下詔徙幽州。

translations.literal: " The emperor grew angrier still and issued an edict exiling him to Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Yang grew angrier still and issued an edict exiling him to Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 後徵還，除銀青光祿大夫，判祠部尚書事。

translations.literal: Later he was recalled and made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and Purple Ribbon, with concurrent charge of the ministry of rites.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was recalled and made grand master of splendid happiness with silver seal and purple ribbon, with concurrent charge of the ministry of rites.

sentences.zh: 帝怒臨漳令嵇曄及舍人李文師，以曄賜薛豐洛、文師賜崔士順為奴。

translations.literal: The emperor in anger toward Linzhang magistrate Ji Ye and palace attendant Li Wenshi gave Ye as slave to Xue Fengluo and Wenshi as slave to Cui Shishun.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang in anger toward Linzhang magistrate Ji Ye and palace attendant Li Wenshi gave Ye as slave to Xue Fengluo and Wenshi as slave to Cui Shishun.

sentences.zh: 鄭子默私謂昕曰：「自古無朝士作奴。

translations.literal: Zheng Zimo said privately to Xin: "From antiquity there have been no court gentlemen made slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zimo said privately to Xin, "From antiquity there have been no court gentlemen made slaves.

sentences.zh: 」昕曰：「箕子為之奴，何言無也？

translations.literal: " Xin said: "Jizi became a slave—how say there were none?
translations.idiomatic: " Xin said, "Jizi became a slave—how say there were none?

sentences.zh: 」子默遂以昕言啟顯祖，仍曰：「王元景比陛下於殷紂。

translations.literal: " Zimo then reported Xin's words to Gao Yang, adding: "Wang Yuanjing compares Your Majesty to King Zhou of Shang.
translations.idiomatic: " Zimo then reported Xin's words to Gao Yang, adding, "Wang Yuanjing compares Your Majesty to King Zhou of Shang.

sentences.zh: 」楊愔微為解之。

translations.literal: " Yang Yin mildly excused him.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Yin mildly excused him.

sentences.zh: 帝謂愔曰：「王元景是爾博士，爾語皆元景所教。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Yin: "Wang Yuanjing is your doctoral mentor; your every word is what Yuanjing taught.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang said to Yin, "Wang Yuanjing is your doctoral mentor; your every word is what Yuanjing taught.

sentences.zh: 」帝後與朝臣酣飲，昕稱病不至。

translations.literal: " Later the emperor drank deep with the court ministers; Xin pleaded illness and did not attend.
translations.idiomatic: " Later Gao Yang drank deep with the court ministers; Xin pleaded illness and did not attend.

sentences.zh: 帝遣騎執之，見方搖膝吟詠，遂斬於御前，投尸漳水，天保十年也。

translations.literal: The emperor sent riders to seize him; they found him swaying his knees and chanting poetry; he was beheaded before the throne, the corpse cast into the Zhang River—in the tenth year of Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang sent riders to seize him; they found him swaying his knees and chanting poetry; he was beheaded before the throne, the corpse cast into the Zhang River—in the tenth year of Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子顗。

translations.literal: His son Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan.

sentences.zh: 昕母清河崔氏，學識有風訓，生九子，並風流蘊藉，世號王氏九龍。

translations.literal: Xin's mother was a Lady Cui of Qinghe, learned and with moral instruction; she bore nine sons, all cultured and refined—the age called them the Nine Dragons of the Wang house.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's mother was a Lady Cui of Qinghe, learned and with moral instruction; she bore nine sons, all cultured and refined—the age called them the Nine Dragons of the Wang house.

sentences.zh: 弟晞，字叔朗，小名沙彌。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xi, styled Shulang, childhood name Shamini.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xi, styled Shulang, childhood name Shamini.

sentences.zh: 幼而孝謹，淹雅有器度，好學不倦，美容儀，有風則。

translations.literal: From childhood he was filial and careful, cultivated and with capacity, tireless in learning, handsome in bearing, with natural dignity.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was filial and careful, cultivated and with capacity, tireless in learning, handsome in bearing, with natural dignity.

sentences.zh: 魏末，隨母兄東適海隅，與邢子良遊處。

translations.literal: At the end of Wei he followed his mother and elder brothers east to the seacoast and kept company with Xing Ziliang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wei he followed his mother and elder brothers east to the seacoast and kept company with Xing Ziliang.

sentences.zh: 子良愛其清悟，與其在洛兩兄書曰：「賢弟彌郎，意識深遠，曠達不羈，簡於造次，言必詣理，吟詠情性，往往麗絕。

translations.literal: Ziliang loved his clarity and insight and wrote to Xi's two elder brothers in Luoyang: "Your worthy younger brother Milang's mind is deep and far-reaching, free and unrestrained, spare even in haste; his words always hit reason; in chanting feeling and nature he is often surpassingly fine.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang loved his clarity and insight and wrote to Xi's two elder brothers in Luoyang, "Your worthy younger brother Milang's mind is deep and far-reaching, free and unrestrained, spare even in haste; his words always hit reason; in chanting feeling and nature he is often surpassingly fine.

sentences.zh: 恐足下方難為兄，不遐慮其不進也。

translations.literal: I fear you gentlemen will hardly be his match as elder brothers and need not worry that he will not advance.
translations.idiomatic: I fear you gentlemen will hardly be his match as elder brothers and need not worry that he will not advance.

sentences.zh: 」魏永安初，第二兄暉聘梁，啟晞釋褐除員外散騎侍郎，徵署廣平王開府功曹史。

translations.literal: " At the beginning of Yong'an in Wei, his second elder brother Hui was betrothed to Liang; he memorialized that Xi be released from commoner status and made Attendant Cavalier, and Xi was summoned to serve as recorder on the staff of Prince of Guangping's opening office.
translations.idiomatic: " At the beginning of Yong'an in Wei, his second elder brother Hui was betrothed to Liang; he memorialized that Xi be released from commoner status and made attendant cavalier, and Xi was summoned to serve as recorder on the staff of Prince of Guangping's opening office.

sentences.zh: 晞願養母，竟不受署。

translations.literal: Xi wished to support his mother and in the end did not accept appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Xi wished to support his mother and in the end did not accept appointment.

sentences.zh: 母終後，仍屬遷鄴。

translations.literal: After his mother died he still went with the move to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died he still went with the move to Ye.

sentences.zh: 遨遊鞏洛，悅其山水，與范陽盧元明、鉅鹿魏季景結侶同契，往天陵山，浩然有終焉之志。

translations.literal: Roaming in Gong and Luo, he delighted in the mountains and waters; with Lu Yuanming of Fanyang and Wei Jijing of Julu he formed a bond of like minds and went to Tianling Mountain, with vast resolve to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: Roaming in Gong and Luo, he delighted in the mountains and waters; with Lu Yuanming of Fanyang and Wei Jijing of Julu he formed a bond of like minds and went to Tianling Mountain, with vast resolve to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 及西魏將獨孤信入洛，署為開府記室。

translations.literal: When Western Wei general Dugu Xin entered Luoyang, he appointed Xi recorder on his opening staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Western Wei general Dugu Xin entered Luoyang, he appointed Xi recorder on his opening staff.

sentences.zh: 晞稱先被犬傷，困篤不起。

translations.literal: Xi claimed he had earlier been bitten by a dog and was gravely ill and could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Xi claimed he had earlier been bitten by a dog and was gravely ill and could not rise.

sentences.zh: 有故人疑其所傷非猘，書勸令起。

translations.literal: An old friend doubted the wound was not from a mad dog and wrote urging him to get up.
translations.idiomatic: An old friend doubted the wound was not from a mad dog and wrote urging him to get up.

sentences.zh: 晞復書曰：「辱告存念，見令起疾，循復眷旨，似疑吾所傷未必是猘。

translations.literal: Xi wrote back: "I am shamed by your care in asking after me and your order to rise from illness; following and pondering your kind intent, you seem to doubt that my wound may not have been from a mad dog.
translations.idiomatic: Xi wrote back, "I am shamed by your care in asking after me and your order to rise from illness; following and pondering your kind intent, you seem to doubt that my wound may not have been from a mad dog.

sentences.zh: 吾豈願其必猘，但理契無疑耳。

translations.literal: Would I wish it must have been mad? Only that reason admits no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Would I wish it must have been mad? Only that reason admits no doubt.

sentences.zh: 就足下疑之，亦有過說。

translations.literal: As for your doubting it, there is also overstatement.
translations.idiomatic: As for your doubting it, there is also overstatement.

sentences.zh: 足下旣疑其非猘，亦可疑其是猘，其疑半矣。

translations.literal: Since you doubt it was not mad, you may also doubt it was mad—your doubt is already half.
translations.idiomatic: Since you doubt it was not mad, you may also doubt it was mad—your doubt is already half.

sentences.zh: 若疑其是猘而營護，雖非犭制亦無損，疑其非猘而不療，儻是猘則難救。

translations.literal: If you doubt it was mad and nurse the wound, though it was not mad there is no harm; if you doubt it was not mad and do not treat it, perchance it was mad and then it is hard to save.
translations.idiomatic: If you doubt it was mad and nurse the wound, though it was not mad there is no harm; if you doubt it was not mad and do not treat it, perchance it was mad and then it is hard to save.

sentences.zh: 然則過療則致萬全，過不療或至死。

translations.literal: Thus overtreatment brings ten thousandfold safety; overt refusal of treatment may bring death.
translations.idiomatic: Thus overtreatment brings ten thousandfold safety; overt refusal of treatment may bring death.

sentences.zh: 若王晞無可惜也，則不足取，旣取之，便是可惜。

translations.literal: If Wang Xi were not worth sparing, then he should not be taken; since he is taken, he is worth sparing.
translations.idiomatic: If Wang Xi were not worth sparing, then he should not be taken; since he is taken, he is worth sparing.

sentences.zh: 奈何奪其萬全，任其或死。

translations.literal: How can you strip him of ten thousandfold safety and leave him to possible death?
translations.idiomatic: How can you strip him of ten thousandfold safety and leave him to possible death?

sentences.zh: 且將軍威德所被，飈飛霧襲，方掩八竑，豈在一介。

translations.literal: Moreover the general's prestige and virtue cover all; wind flies and mist strikes, about to enfold the eight reaches—surely not for one man alone.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the general's prestige and virtue cover all; wind flies and mist strikes, about to enfold the eight reaches—surely not for one man alone.

sentences.zh: 若必從隗始，先須濟其生靈。

translations.literal: If you must begin from the start, first you must succor the living people.
translations.idiomatic: If you must begin from the start, first you must succor the living people.

sentences.zh: 足下何不從容為將軍言也？

translations.literal: Why do you not speak to the general at leisure on my behalf?
translations.idiomatic: Why do you not speak to the general at leisure on my behalf?

sentences.zh: 」於是方得見寬。

translations.literal: " Only then was he granted leniency.
translations.idiomatic: " Only then was he granted leniency.

sentences.zh: 俄而信返，晞遂歸鄴。

translations.literal: Soon Dugu Xin returned west; Xi then went back to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Dugu Xin returned west; Xi then went back to Ye.

sentences.zh: 齊神武訪朝廷子弟忠孝謹密者，令與諸子遊。

translations.literal: Gao Huan sought sons of the court who were loyal, filial, careful, and steady, to keep company with his sons.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan sought sons of the court who were loyal, filial, careful, and steady, to keep company with his sons.

sentences.zh: 晞與清河崔瞻、頓丘李度、范陽盧正通首應此選。

translations.literal: Xi and Cui Zhan of Qinghe, Li Du of Dunqiu, and Lu Zhengtong of Fanyang were the first chosen for this.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and Cui Zhan of Qinghe, Li Du of Dunqiu, and Lu Zhengtong of Fanyang were the first chosen for this.

sentences.zh: 文襄時為大將軍，握晞等手曰：「我弟並向成長，志識未定，近善狎惡，不能不移。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng was then grand general; he took Xi and the others by the hand and said: "My younger brothers are all growing up; their aims and knowledge are not yet fixed—near goodness they draw close, near evil they cannot but shift.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng was then grand general; he took Xi and the others by the hand and said, "My younger brothers are all growing up; their aims and knowledge are not yet fixed—near goodness they draw close, near evil they cannot but shift.

sentences.zh: 吾弟成立，不負義方，卿祿位常亞吾弟。

translations.literal: If my younger brothers are established, they will not betray righteous teaching; your rank and salary will always rank just below my younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: If my younger brothers are established, they will not betray righteous teaching; your rank and salary will always rank just below my younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 若茍使迴邪，致相詿誤，罪及門族，非止一身。

translations.literal: If you would make them turn crooked and lead one another astray, guilt will reach the clan—not you alone.
translations.idiomatic: If you would make them turn crooked and lead one another astray, guilt will reach the clan—not you alone.

sentences.zh: 」晞隨神武到晉陽，補中外府功曹參軍，帶常山王演友。

translations.literal: " Xi followed Gao Huan to Jinyang, was made staff officer of the inner and outer offices, and attended Prince of Changshan Yan as companion.
translations.idiomatic: " Xi followed Gao Huan to Jinyang, was made staff officer of the inner and outer offices, and attended Prince of Changshan Yan as companion.

sentences.zh: 齊天保初，行太原郡事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao in Qi he acted as administrator of Taiyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao in Qi he acted as administrator of Taiyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 及文宣昏逸，常山王數諫，帝疑王假辭於晞，欲加大辟。

translations.literal: When Gao Yang grew dissolute, Prince of Changshan remonstrated repeatedly; the emperor suspected the prince borrowed his words from Xi and wished to impose the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yang grew dissolute, Prince of Changshan remonstrated repeatedly; Gao Yang suspected the prince borrowed his words from Xi and wished to impose the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 王私謂晞曰：「博士，明日當作一條事，為欲相活，亦圖自全，宜深體勿怪。

translations.literal: The prince said privately to Xi: "Doctor, tomorrow you must do one thing—for I mean to keep you alive and also to save myself; understand deeply and do not take it amiss.
translations.idiomatic: The prince said privately to Xi, "Doctor, tomorrow you must do one thing—for I mean to keep you alive and also to save myself; understand deeply and do not take it amiss.

sentences.zh: 」乃於衆中杖晞二十。

translations.literal: " He then had Xi beaten twenty strokes before the assembly.
translations.idiomatic: " He then had Xi beaten twenty strokes before the assembly.

sentences.zh: 帝尋發怒，聞晞得杖，以故不殺，髡鉗配甲坊。

translations.literal: The emperor soon flared in anger; hearing Xi had been beaten, on that account he did not kill him but shaved his head, put him in fetters, and assigned him to the armorer's ward.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang soon flared in anger; hearing Xi had been beaten, on that account he did not kill him but shaved his head, put him in fetters, and assigned him to the armorer's ward.

sentences.zh: 居三年，王又固諫爭，大被毆撻，閉口不食。

translations.literal: After three years the prince again remonstrated firmly; he was beaten severely, closed his mouth and would not eat.
translations.idiomatic: After three years the prince again remonstrated firmly; he was beaten severely, closed his mouth and would not eat.

sentences.zh: 太后極憂之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was deeply grieved.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was deeply grieved.

sentences.zh: 帝謂左右曰：「儻小兒死，奈我老母何？

translations.literal: The emperor said to those about him: "If the boy dies, what of my old mother?
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang said to those about him, "If the boy dies, what of my old mother?

sentences.zh: 」於是每問王疾，謂曰：「努力強食，當以王晞還汝。

translations.literal: " He then each day inquired after the prince's illness and told him: "Strive and force yourself to eat; I will give Wang Xi back to you.
translations.idiomatic: " He then each day inquired after the prince's illness and told him, "Strive and force yourself to eat; I will give Wang Xi back to you.

sentences.zh: 」乃釋晞令往。

translations.literal: " He released Xi and sent him to the prince.
translations.idiomatic: " He released Xi and sent him to the prince.

sentences.zh: 王抱晞曰：「吾氣力綴然，恐不復相見。

translations.literal: The prince embraced Xi and said: "My breath and strength are failing; I fear we shall not meet again.
translations.idiomatic: The prince embraced Xi and said, "My breath and strength are failing; I fear we shall not meet again.

sentences.zh: 」晞流涕曰：「天道神明，豈令殿下遂斃此舍。

translations.literal: " Xi wept and said: "Heaven's way and the spirits—how could they let Your Highness die in this house!
translations.idiomatic: " Xi wept and said, "Heaven's way and the spirits—how could they let Your Highness die in this house!

sentences.zh: 至尊親為人兄，尊為人主，安可與校計。

translations.literal: The Supreme One is elder brother in person and sovereign in rank—how can you contend with him?
translations.idiomatic: The Supreme One is elder brother in person and sovereign in rank—how can you contend with him?

sentences.zh: 殿下不食，太后亦不食，殿下縱不自惜，不惜太后乎？

translations.literal: Your Highness will not eat; the empress dowager will not eat either—if Your Highness will not spare yourself, will you not spare the empress dowager?
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness will not eat; the empress dowager will not eat either—if Your Highness will not spare yourself, will you not spare the empress dowager?

sentences.zh: 」言未卒，王強坐而飯。

translations.literal: " Before he finished speaking, the prince forced himself to sit up and eat.
translations.idiomatic: " Before he finished speaking, the prince forced himself to sit up and eat.

sentences.zh: 晞由是得免徙，還為王友。

translations.literal: Xi was thereby spared exile and returned as the prince's companion.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was thereby spared exile and returned as the prince's companion.

sentences.zh: 王復錄尚書事，新除官者必詣王謝職，去必辭。

translations.literal: The prince again recorded Masters of Writing affairs; newly appointed officials had to visit the prince to thank him for their posts, and on leaving had to take leave.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Changshan again recorded Masters of Writing affairs; newly appointed officials had to visit him to thank him for their posts, and on leaving had to take leave.

sentences.zh: 晞言於王曰：「受爵天朝，拜恩私第，自古以為干紀。

translations.literal: Xi said to the prince: "To receive rank from the heavenly court and pay thanks at a private residence has from antiquity been held a breach of protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi said to the prince, "To receive rank from the heavenly court and pay thanks at a private residence has from antiquity been held a breach of protocol.

sentences.zh: 朝廷文武，出入辭謝，宜一約絕。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials of the court, coming and going with thanks and farewells — it should all be stopped at once.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials of the court, coming and going with thanks and farewells — it should all be stopped at once.

sentences.zh: 主上顒顒，賴殿下扶翼。

translations.literal: The sovereign is attentive; he relies on Your Highness to support him.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign is attentive; he relies on Your Highness to support him.

sentences.zh: 」王納焉。

translations.literal: " The prince accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince accepted this.

sentences.zh: 常從容謂晞曰：「主上起居不恒，卿耳目所具，吾豈可以前逢一怒，遂爾結舌。

translations.literal: He often said calmly to Xi: "The sovereign's conduct is unsteady; you see and hear what he does — can I really stay silent forever because I once provoked his anger?
translations.idiomatic: He often said calmly to Wang Xi, "The sovereign's conduct is unsteady; you see and hear what he does — can I really stay silent forever because I once provoked his anger?

sentences.zh: 卿宜為撰諫草，吾當伺便極諫。

translations.literal: You should draft a memorial of remonstrance; I will seize a suitable moment and remonstrate to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: You should draft a memorial of remonstrance; I will seize a suitable moment and remonstrate to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 」晞遂條十餘事以呈。

translations.literal: " Xi then set out more than ten items and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Xi then set out more than ten items and presented them.

sentences.zh: 切諫王曰：「今朝廷乃爾，欲學介子匹夫輕一朝之命，狂藥令人不自覺，刀箭豈復識親疏，一旦禍出理外，將奈殿下家業何，奈皇太后何！

translations.literal: He remonstrated sharply with the prince: "The court is now like this — do you wish to follow some reckless commoner who treats a morning's life lightly? Madness-drug makes a man unaware of himself; blade and arrow no longer know kin from stranger. If disaster suddenly comes from beyond reason, what of Your Highness's household estate — what of the empress dowager!
translations.idiomatic: He remonstrated sharply with the prince, "The court is now like this — do you wish to follow some reckless commoner who treats a morning's life lightly? Madness-drug makes a man unaware of himself; blade and arrow no longer know kin from stranger. If disaster suddenly comes from beyond reason, what of Your Highness's household estate — what of the empress dowager!

sentences.zh: 乞且將順，日慎一日。

translations.literal: I beg you for now to yield and go along, and be more careful day by day.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you for now to yield and go along, and be more careful day by day.

sentences.zh: 」王歔欷不自勝，曰：「乃至是乎？

translations.literal: " The prince sobbed uncontrollably and said: "Has it come to this?
translations.idiomatic: " The prince sobbed uncontrollably and said, "Has it come to this?

sentences.zh: 」明日見晞曰：「吾長夜九思，今便息意。

translations.literal: " Next day he saw Xi and said: "I thought all night; now my mind is at rest.
translations.idiomatic: " Next day he saw Wang Xi and said, "I thought all night; now my mind is at rest.

sentences.zh: 」便命火對晞焚之。

translations.literal: " He ordered fire and burned the draft before Xi.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered fire and burned the draft before Wang Xi.

sentences.zh: 後王承間苦諫，遂至忤旨。

translations.literal: Later the prince seized an opening and remonstrated bitterly, until he offended the sovereign's will.
translations.idiomatic: Later the prince seized an opening and remonstrated bitterly, until he offended the sovereign's will.

sentences.zh: 帝使力士反接，拔白刃註頸，罵曰：「小子何知，欲以吏才非我，是誰教汝？

translations.literal: The emperor had brawny men twist his arms behind him, drew a bare blade and set it to his neck, and cursed: "What does a stripling know — you mean to deny me with clerkly talent; who taught you?
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang had brawny men twist his arms behind him, drew a bare blade and set it to his neck, and cursed, "What does a stripling know — you mean to deny me with clerkly talent; who taught you?

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「天下噤口，除臣誰敢有言。

translations.literal: " The prince said: "The realm holds its tongue; apart from your servant, who dares speak?
translations.idiomatic: " The prince said, "The realm holds its tongue; apart from your servant, who dares speak?

sentences.zh: 」帝催遣捶楚，亂杖抶數十，會醉臥得解。

translations.literal: " The emperor urged them on to beat him; they flogged him with clubs dozens of times; he happened to be drunk and asleep and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Yang urged them on to beat him; they flogged him with clubs dozens of times; he happened to be drunk and asleep and was spared.

sentences.zh: 爾後褻黷之好，遍於宗戚，所往留連，俾晝作夜，唯常山邸多無適而去。

translations.literal: Thereafter his lewd pursuits spread among kin; wherever he went he lingered, turning day into night — only at the Changshan residence he often found no fit occasion and left.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Gao Yang's lewd pursuits spread among kin; wherever he went he lingered, turning day into night — only at the Changshan residence he often found no fit occasion and left.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，濟南嗣立。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Jinan succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yang died, Prince of Jinan succeeded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 王謂晞曰：「一人垂拱，吾曹亦保優閑。

translations.literal: The prince said to Xi: "One man holds court at ease; we too shall keep our ease.
translations.idiomatic: The prince said to Wang Xi, "One man holds court at ease; we too shall keep our ease.

sentences.zh: 」因言朝廷寬仁慈恕，真守文良主。

translations.literal: " He added that the court was lenient, benevolent, and forgiving — a true heir who guarded the patrimony, a good ruler.
translations.idiomatic: " He added that the court was lenient, benevolent, and forgiving — a true heir who guarded the patrimony, a good ruler.

sentences.zh: 晞曰：「天保享祚，東宮委一胡人，今卒覽萬機，駕馭雄桀。

translations.literal: Xi said: "In the Tianbao era fortunes held; the eastern palace was entrusted to a barbarian. Now he suddenly oversees all affairs, driving fierce men.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi said, "In the Tianbao era fortunes held; the eastern palace was entrusted to a barbarian. Now he suddenly oversees all affairs, driving fierce men.

sentences.zh: 如聖德幼沖，未堪多難，而使他姓出納詔命，必權有所歸。

translations.literal: If His Sagehood is young and not equal to many trials, yet others hand in and out the imperial edicts, power is sure to settle somewhere.
translations.idiomatic: If His Sagehood is young and not equal to many trials, yet others hand in and out the imperial edicts, power is sure to settle somewhere.

sentences.zh: 殿下雖欲守藩職，其可得也！

translations.literal: Though Your Highness wish to keep to princely duty, can you?
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Highness wish to keep to princely duty, can you?

sentences.zh: 遐令得遂沖退，自審保家祚得靈長不？

translations.literal: If far-off orders let you retire in modesty, do you yourself judge that the house and throne can endure long?
translations.idiomatic: If far-off orders let you retire in modesty, do you yourself judge that the house and throne can endure long?

sentences.zh: 」王默然思念，久之曰：「何以處我？

translations.literal: " The prince fell silent in thought; after a long while said: "How am I to be placed?
translations.idiomatic: " The prince fell silent in thought; after a long while said, "How am I to be placed?

sentences.zh: 」晞曰：「周公抱成王朝諸侯，攝政七年，然後復子明辟，幸有故事，惟殿下慮之。

translations.literal: " Xi said: "The Duke of Zhou held King Cheng in his arms and received the feudal lords, regent seven years, then returned the government and made the son clear sovereign — fortunately there is precedent; only Your Highness must weigh it.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Xi said, "The Duke of Zhou held King Cheng in his arms and received the feudal lords, regent seven years, then returned the government and made the son clear sovereign — fortunately there is precedent; only Your Highness must weigh it.

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「我安敢自擬周公。

translations.literal: " The prince said: "How dare I liken myself to the Duke of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince said, "How dare I liken myself to the Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 」晞曰：「殿下今日地望，欲避周公得耶？

translations.literal: " Xi said: "Your Highness's standing today — can you avoid the Duke of Zhou?
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Xi said, "Your Highness's standing today — can you avoid the Duke of Zhou?

sentences.zh: 」王不答。

translations.literal: " The prince did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince did not answer.

sentences.zh: 帝臨發，勑王從駕，除晞幷州長史。

translations.literal: When the emperor set out, he ordered the prince to follow the carriage; Xi was made chief administrator of Bing.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor set out, he ordered the prince to follow the carriage; Wang Xi was made chief administrator of Bing.

sentences.zh: 及王至鄴，誅楊、燕等，詔以王為大丞相、都督中外諸軍事，督攝文武，還至幷。

translations.literal: When the prince reached Ye, Yang, Yan and others were executed; an edict made the prince grand chancellor, commander-in-chief of all armies within and without, overseeing civil and military affairs; he returned to Bing.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince reached Ye, Yang Yin, Murong Yan and others were executed; an edict made him grand chancellor, commander-in-chief of all armies within and without, overseeing civil and military affairs; he returned to Bing.

sentences.zh: 乃延晞謂曰：「不早用卿言，使群小弄權，幾至傾覆。

translations.literal: He then summoned Xi and said: "Because I did not heed your words early, petty men wielded power and I nearly came to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned Wang Xi and said, "Because I did not heed your words early, petty men wielded power and I nearly came to ruin.

sentences.zh: 今君側雖獲暫清，終當何以處我？

translations.literal: Though by the ruler's side it is briefly cleared, in the end how am I to be placed?
translations.idiomatic: Though by the ruler's side it is briefly cleared, in the end how am I to be placed?

sentences.zh: 」晞曰：「殿下將往時地位，猶可以名教出處。

translations.literal: " Xi said: "Your Highness's former standing could still be weighed by name and teaching in going forth and withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Xi said, "Your Highness's former standing could still be weighed by name and teaching in going forth and withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 今日事勢，遂關天時，非復人理所及。

translations.literal: Today's situation turns on heaven's timing; it is no longer within human reason.
translations.idiomatic: Today's situation turns on heaven's timing; it is no longer within human reason.

sentences.zh: 」有頃，奏趙郡王叡為左長史，晞為司馬。

translations.literal: " Before long it was memorialized that Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui be left chief administrator, and Xi be chief marshal.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long it was memorialized that Prince of Zhao Commandery Gao Rui be left chief administrator, and Wang Xi be chief marshal.

sentences.zh: 每夜載入，晝則不與語，以晞儒緩，恐不允武將之意。

translations.literal: Each night he was brought in by carriage; by day they did not speak — because Xi was scholarly and slow, fearing he would not suit the generals' mind.
translations.idiomatic: Each night he was brought in by carriage; by day they did not speak — because Wang Xi was scholarly and slow, fearing he would not suit the generals' mind.

sentences.zh: 後進晞密室曰：「比王侯諸貴每見煎迫，言我違天不祥，恐當或有變起，吾正欲以法繩之。

translations.literal: Later the prince entered a private room and said: "Of late the princes and great men each press me, saying I go against heaven and invite ill fortune — fearing some change may rise. I mean to hold them by law.
translations.idiomatic: Later the prince entered a private room and said, "Of late the princes and great men each press me, saying I go against heaven and invite ill fortune — fearing some change may rise. I mean to hold them by law.

sentences.zh: 」晞曰：「朝廷比者疏遠親戚，寧思骨血之重。

translations.literal: " Xi said: "The court of late has kept kin at distance — does it consider the weight of bone and blood?
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Xi said, "The court of late has kept kin at distance — does it consider the weight of bone and blood?

sentences.zh: 殿下倉卒所行，非復人臣之事，芒刺在背，交戟入頸，上下相疑，何由可久。

translations.literal: Your Highness's hasty acts are no longer the matter of a minister; a thorn in the back, crossed halberds at the neck — above and below doubting each other; how can it last?
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness's hasty acts are no longer the matter of a minister; a thorn in the back, crossed halberds at the neck — above and below doubting each other; how can it last?

sentences.zh: 且天道不恒，虧盈叠至，神幾變化，肹蚃斯集。

translations.literal: Moreover heaven's way is not constant; loss and gain pile on; spirit and omen shift — subtle signs gather.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover heaven's way is not constant; loss and gain pile on; spirit and omen shift — subtle signs gather.

sentences.zh: 雖執謙挹，粃糠神器，便是違上玄之意，墜先帝之基。

translations.literal: Though you hold modesty and restraint, to treat the sacred vessel like chaff is to go against the Supreme One's intent and wreck the late emperor's foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Though you hold modesty and restraint, to treat the sacred vessel like chaff is to go against heaven's intent and wreck the late emperor's foundation.

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「卿何敢發非所宜言，須致卿於法。

translations.literal: " The prince said: "How dare you speak what should not be spoken — I must bring you to law.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince said, "How dare you speak what should not be spoken — I must bring you to law.

sentences.zh: 」晞曰：「竊謂天時人事，同無異揆，是以冒犯雷霆，不憚斧鉞。

translations.literal: " Xi said: "I hold that heaven's timing and human affairs share one measure; therefore I offend the thunder, fearless of axe and halberd.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Xi said, "I hold that heaven's timing and human affairs share one measure; therefore I offend the thunder, fearless of axe and halberd.

sentences.zh: 今日得披肝膽，抑亦神明攸贊。

translations.literal: Today I may lay bare heart and liver — perhaps the spirits also approve.
translations.idiomatic: Today I may lay bare heart and liver — perhaps the spirits also approve.

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「拯難匡輔，方俟聖哲，吾何敢私議，幸勿多言。

translations.literal: " The prince said: "To rescue difficulty and set up support waits for a sage; how dare I debate in private — please speak no more.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince said, "To rescue difficulty and set up support waits for a sage; how dare I debate in private — please speak no more.

sentences.zh: 」尋有詔以丞相任重，普進府僚一班，晞以司馬領吏部郎中。

translations.literal: " Soon an edict said the chancellor's burden was heavy and all staff advanced one grade; Xi as chief marshal also held the post of gentleman in the ministry of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon an edict said the chancellor's burden was heavy and all staff advanced one grade; Wang Xi as chief marshal also held the post of gentleman in the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 丞相從事中郎陸杳將出使，臨別握晞手曰：「相王功格區宇，天下樂推，歌謠滿道，物無異望。

translations.literal: Chancellor attendant Lu Yao was about to go on mission; on parting he clasped Xi's hand and said: "The great prince's merit fills the realm, the realm joyfully urges him on, songs fill the roads, things have no different wish.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor attendant Lu Yao was about to go on mission; on parting he clasped Wang Xi's hand and said, "The great prince's merit fills the realm, the realm joyfully urges him on, songs fill the roads, things have no different wish.

sentences.zh: 杳等願披赤心，而忽奉外使，無由面盡短誠，寸心謹以仰白。

translations.literal: We wish to bare our loyal hearts, but suddenly receive outer mission, with no face-to-face way to speak our brief loyalty — our inch of heart we respectfully raise to you.
translations.idiomatic: We wish to bare our loyal hearts, but suddenly receive outer mission, with no face-to-face way to speak our brief loyalty — our inch of heart we respectfully raise to you.

sentences.zh: 」晞尋述杳言。

translations.literal: " Xi soon repeated Yao's words.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Xi soon repeated Yao's words.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「若內外咸有異望，趙彥深朝夕左右，何因都無所論？

translations.literal: The prince said: "If inside and outside alike have different hopes, Zhao Yanshen is morning and evening at my side — why has he never spoken of it?
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "If inside and outside alike have different hopes, Zhao Yanshen is morning and evening at my side — why has he never spoken of it?

sentences.zh: 自以卿意試密與言之。

translations.literal: Try my meaning and speak of it secretly to him.
translations.idiomatic: Try my meaning and speak of it secretly to him.

sentences.zh: 」晞以事隙問彥深，彥深曰：「我比亦驚此音謠，每欲陳聞，則口噤心戰。

translations.literal: " Xi seized a moment and asked Yanshen; Yanshen said: "I too of late was startled by these songs; each time I wished to report, my mouth locked and my heart trembled.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Xi seized a moment and asked Yanshen; Yanshen said, "I too of late was startled by these songs; each time I wished to report, my mouth locked and my heart trembled.

sentences.zh: 弟旣發論，吾亦昧死一披肝膽。

translations.literal: Younger brother has now begun the theme; I too will risk death and bare heart and liver once.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother has now begun the theme; I too will risk death and bare heart and liver once.

sentences.zh: 」因亦同勸。

translations.literal: " He then likewise urged him on.
translations.idiomatic: " He then likewise urged him on.

sentences.zh: 是時諸王公將校四方岳牧表陳符命。

translations.literal: At that time the princes and generals and the four quarters' governors memorialized the mandate's signs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the princes and generals and the four quarters' governors memorialized the mandate's signs.

sentences.zh: 乾明元年八月，昭帝踐祚。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Ganming, Emperor Xiaozhao ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Ganming, Emperor Xiaozhao ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 九月，除晞散騎常侍，仍領兼吏部郎中。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Xi was made attendant cavalier; he still held concurrently gentleman in the ministry of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Wang Xi was made attendant cavalier; he still held concurrently gentleman in the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 後因奏事罷，帝從容曰：比日何為自同外客，略不可見。

translations.literal: Later, when a memorial audience ended, the emperor said calmly: "Of late why do you act like an outsider guest — you are hardly to be seen at all.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when a memorial audience ended, the emperor said calmly, "Of late why do you act like an outsider guest — you are hardly to be seen at all.

sentences.zh: 自今假非局司，但有所懷，隨宜作一牒，候少隙即徑進也。

translations.literal: From now, unless it is office business, whenever you have something in mind, make a slip as fits and when a brief opening appears bring it straight in.
translations.idiomatic: From now, unless it is office business, whenever you have something in mind, make a slip as fits and when a brief opening appears bring it straight in.

sentences.zh: 」因勑尚書陽休之、鴻臚卿崔劼等三人，每日本職務罷，並入東廊，共舉錄歷代廢禮墜樂、職司廢置、朝饗異同、輿服增損。

translations.literal: " He ordered Director of the Masters of Writing Yang Xiuzhi, Director of Ceremonies Cui Jie, and one other — three men — each day when their proper duties ended, all to enter the eastern corridor and together record rites fallen and music lost through the ages, offices abolished, court sacrifice differences, carriage dress additions and subtractions.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered director of the Masters of Writing Yang Xiuzhi, director of ceremonies Cui Jie, and one other — three men — each day when their proper duties ended, all to enter the eastern corridor and together record rites fallen and music lost through the ages, offices abolished, court sacrifice differences, carriage dress additions and subtractions.

sentences.zh: 或道德高儁，久在沉淪；

translations.literal: Or men of lofty virtue long sunk in obscurity;
translations.idiomatic: Or men of lofty virtue long sunk in obscurity;

sentences.zh: 或巧言眩俗，妖邪害政，爰及田市舟車、徵稅通塞、婚葬儀軌、貴賤齊衰，有不便於時而古今行用不已者，或自古利用而當今毀棄者，悉令詳思，以漸條奏，未待頓備，遇憶續聞。

translations.literal: or clever words dazzling the vulgar and evil spirits harming government — reaching taxes on fields, markets, boats and carts, levies open or blocked, marriage and burial rules, noble and base full mourning — whatever was inconvenient in the time yet used unceasingly from old and new, or useful in antiquity yet destroyed today: all were to think in detail, report item by item in time, not wait until all was ready; when memory returned, continue the report.
translations.idiomatic: or clever words dazzling the vulgar and evil spirits harming government — reaching taxes on fields, markets, boats and carts, levies open or blocked, marriage and burial rules, noble and base full mourning — whatever was inconvenient in the time yet used unceasingly from old and new, or useful in antiquity yet destroyed today: all were to think in detail, report item by item in time, not wait until all was ready; when memory returned, continue the report.

sentences.zh: 朝晡給與御食，畢景聽遠。

translations.literal: Morning and evening they were given imperial food; until sunset they listened afar.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening they were given imperial food; until sunset they listened afar.

sentences.zh: 時百官請建東宮，勑未許。

translations.literal: At the time the hundred officials asked to establish the eastern palace; the edict did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the hundred officials asked to establish the eastern palace; the edict did not grant it.

sentences.zh: 每令晞就東堂監視太子冠服，導引趨拜。

translations.literal: Each time Xi was sent to the eastern hall to oversee the crown prince's cap and robe, guiding and leading his pace in bowing.
translations.idiomatic: Each time Wang Xi was sent to the eastern hall to oversee the crown prince's cap and robe, guiding and leading his pace in bowing.

sentences.zh: 為太子太傅，晞以局司奉璽綬。

translations.literal: He was made grand tutor of the crown prince; Xi as office-holder received the seal and sash.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand tutor of the crown prince; Wang Xi as office-holder received the seal and sash.

sentences.zh: 皇太子釋奠，又兼中庶子。

translations.literal: When the crown prince performed the capping sacrifice, he was also concurrently palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince performed the capping sacrifice, he was also concurrently palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 帝謂曰：「今旣當劇職，不得尋常舒慢也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Now that you hold urgent office, you cannot as usual be leisurely and slow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Now that you hold urgent office, you cannot as usual be leisurely and slow.

sentences.zh: 帝將北征，勑問外間比何所聞。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to campaign north; he ordered inquiry what was heard outside lately.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to campaign north; he ordered inquiry what was heard outside lately.

sentences.zh: 晞曰：「道路傳言，車駕將行。

translations.literal: Xi said: "On the roads they say the imperial carriage will march.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi said, "On the roads they say the imperial carriage will march.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「庫莫奚南侵，我未經親戎，因此聊欲習武。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "The Kumo Xi raid south; I have not myself led arms — therefore I wish for the moment to drill soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "The Kumo Xi raid south; I have not myself led arms — therefore I wish for the moment to drill soldiers.

sentences.zh: 」晞曰：「鑾駕巡狩，為復可爾，若輕有驅使，恐天下失望。

translations.literal: " Xi said: "Imperial tours for inspection may still pass; if lightly there is dispatch, I fear the realm will lose hope.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Xi said, "Imperial tours for inspection may still pass; if lightly there is dispatch, I fear the realm will lose hope.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「此懦夫常慮，吾自當臨時斟酌。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "This is the coward's constant worry; I myself will weigh it when the time comes.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "This is the coward's constant worry; I myself will weigh it when the time comes.

sentences.zh: 」帝使齊帥裴澤、主書蔡暉伺察群下，好相誣枉，朝士呼為裴、蔡。

translations.literal: The emperor had the Qi commander Pei Ze and document clerk Cai Hui spy on the host below, fond of mutual slander; court gentlemen called them Pei and Cai.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had the Qi commander Pei Ze and document clerk Cai Hui spy on the host below, fond of mutual slander; court gentlemen called them Pei and Cai.

sentences.zh: 時二人奏車駕北征後，人言陽休之、王晞數與諸人遊宴，不以公事在懷。

translations.literal: At that time the two reported that after the imperial carriage's northern campaign, people said Yang Xiuzhi and Wang Xi often feasted and wandered with others, not keeping public business in mind.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the two reported that after the imperial carriage's northern campaign, people said Yang Xiuzhi and Wang Xi often feasted and wandered with others, not keeping public business in mind.

sentences.zh: 帝杖休之、晞脛各四十。

translations.literal: The emperor flogged Xiuzhi and Xi each forty blows on the shins.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flogged Xiuzhi and Wang Xi each forty blows on the shins.

sentences.zh: 帝斬人於前，問晞曰：「此人合死不？

translations.literal: The emperor beheaded a man before him and asked Xi: "Does this man deserve death?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor beheaded a man before him and asked Wang Xi, "Does this man deserve death?

sentences.zh: 」晞曰：「罪實合死，但恨其不得死地。

translations.literal: " Xi said: "His crime indeed deserves death — only I regret he did not die in the proper place.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Xi said, "His crime indeed deserves death — only I regret he did not die in the proper place.

sentences.zh: 臣聞刑人於市，與衆棄之，殿廷非殺戮之所。

translations.literal: I hear that punishing men in the market means abandoning them with the crowd; the palace hall is not a place for killing.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that punishing men in the market means abandoning them with the crowd; the palace hall is not a place for killing.

sentences.zh: 」帝改容曰：「自今當為王公改之。」

translations.literal: " The emperor changed countenance and said: "From now I shall change it for the princes.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor changed countenance and said, "From now I shall change it for the princes.

sentences.zh: 帝欲以晞為侍中，苦辭不受。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to make Xi palace attendant; he firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to make Wang Xi palace attendant; he firmly declined and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 或勸晞勿自疏，晞曰：「我少年以來，閱要人多矣，充詘少時，鮮不敗績。

translations.literal: Some urged Xi not to distance himself; Xi said: "From youth I have seen many men in power; puffed up for a little while, few did not end in ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Wang Xi not to distance himself; Wang Xi said, "From youth I have seen many men in power; puffed up for a little while, few did not end in ruin.

sentences.zh: 且性實疏緩，不堪時務，人主恩私，何由可保，萬一披猖，求退無地。

translations.literal: Moreover my nature is truly loose and slow, unfit for the times; a sovereign's private favor — how can it be kept? If by chance I lose restraint, there is nowhere to seek withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover my nature is truly loose and slow, unfit for the times; a sovereign's private favor — how can it be kept? If by chance I lose restraint, there is nowhere to seek withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 非不愛作熱官，但思之爛熟耳。

translations.literal: It is not that I do not love the hot office — I have only chewed it over to the end.
translations.idiomatic: It is not that I do not love the hot office — I have only chewed it over to the end.

sentences.zh: 」百官嘗賜射，晞中的，當得絹，為不書箭，有司不與。

translations.literal: Once the hundred officials were granted an archery contest; Xi hit the target and should have received silk, but because he did not mark his arrow, the office would not give it.
translations.idiomatic: Once the hundred officials were granted an archery contest; Wang Xi hit the target and should have received silk, but because he did not mark his arrow, the office would not give it.

sentences.zh: 晞陶陶然曰：「我今可謂武有餘文不足矣。

translations.literal: Xi said with easy content: "Today I may be called abundant in martial, short in literary.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi said with easy content, "Today I may be called abundant in martial, short in literary.

sentences.zh: 」晞無子，帝將賜之妾，使小黃門就宅宣旨，皇後相聞晞妻。

translations.literal: Xi had no son; the emperor would grant him a concubine; a yellow gate attendant went to his house to announce the edict; the empress also sent word to Xi's wife.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi had no son; the emperor would grant him a concubine; a yellow gate attendant went to his house to announce the edict; the empress also sent word to Wang Xi's wife.

sentences.zh: 晞令妻答，妻終不言，晞以手拊胸而退。

translations.literal: Xi had his wife answer; the wife never spoke; Xi pat his chest with his hand and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi had his wife answer; the wife never spoke; Wang Xi patted his chest with his hand and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之笑。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard it he laughed.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard it he laughed.

sentences.zh: 孝昭崩，哀慕殆不自勝，因以羸敗。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhao died, he mourned almost beyond bearing and fell ill from weakness.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhao died, he mourned almost beyond bearing and fell ill from weakness.

sentences.zh: 武成本忿其儒緩，由是彌嫌之，因奏事大被訶叱，而雅步晏然。

translations.literal: Emperor Wucheng had long resented his scholarly slowness and therefore disliked him the more; on presenting business he was roundly scolded, yet walked with elegant pace, unruffled.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng had long resented his scholarly slowness and therefore disliked him the more; on presenting business he was roundly scolded, yet walked with elegant pace, unruffled.

sentences.zh: 歷東徐州刺史、秘書監。

translations.literal: He passed through posts as governor of eastern Xuzhou and director of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He passed through posts as governor of eastern Xuzhou and director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 武平初，遷大鴻臚，加儀同三司，監修起居注，待詔文林館。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuping he was moved to grand director of ceremonies, given the same ceremonial rank as the three masters, supervised revision of the veritable records, and attended at the Forest of Literary Brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wuping he was moved to grand director of ceremonies, given the same ceremonial rank as the three masters, supervised revision of the veritable records, and attended at the Forest of Literary Brilliance.

sentences.zh: 性閑淡寡欲，雖王事鞅掌，而雅操不移。

translations.literal: His nature was leisurely and light in desire; though kingly affairs pressed thick, his refined conduct did not shift.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was leisurely and light in desire; though kingly affairs pressed thick, his refined conduct did not shift.

sentences.zh: 在幷州，雖戎馬填閭，未嘗以世務為累。

translations.literal: In Bing Province, though war horses filled the lanes, he never took worldly business as a burden.
translations.idiomatic: In Bing Province, though war horses filled the lanes, he never took worldly business as a burden.

sentences.zh: 良辰美景，嘯詠遨遊，登臨山水，以談讌為事，人士謂之物外司馬。

translations.literal: On fine days and fair scenes he would chant and roam, climb hills and waters, making conversation and feasts his affair; gentlemen called him the marshal beyond things.
translations.idiomatic: On fine days and fair scenes he would chant and roam, climb hills and waters, making conversation and feasts his affair; gentlemen called him the marshal beyond things.

sentences.zh: 常詣晉祠，賦詩曰：「日落應歸去，魚鳥見留連。

translations.literal: He often visited the Jin shrine and composed a poem: "The sun sets — I ought to go home; fish and birds seem to linger.
translations.idiomatic: He often visited the Jin shrine and composed a poem: "The sun sets — I ought to go home; fish and birds seem to linger.

sentences.zh: 」忽有相王使至，召晞不時至。

translations.literal: Suddenly a messenger of the great prince arrived; he summoned Xi, who did not come at once.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a messenger of the great prince arrived; he summoned Wang Xi, who did not come at once.

sentences.zh: 明日丞相西閤祭酒盧思道謂晞曰：「昨被召已朱顏，得不以魚鳥致怪？

translations.literal: The next day the chancellor's Western Pavilion Libationer Lu Sidao said to Xi, "Yesterday when you were summoned your face was already flushed — are the fish and birds not to blame for giving offense?"
translations.idiomatic: Next day Lu Sidao, libationer of the chancellor's Western Pavilion, said to Xi, "When you were summoned yesterday your face was already flushed — surely the fish and birds are not to blame for the offense?"

sentences.zh: 」晞緩笑曰：「昨晚陶然，頗以酒漿被責，卿輩亦是留連之一物，豈直在魚鳥而已。

translations.literal: " Xi smiled slowly and said, "Last night I was quite at ease; I was rather reproached for wine. You gentlemen too are among the things that detain one — surely not only fish and birds."
translations.idiomatic: " Xi smiled slowly. "Last night I was quite at ease, and got a fair scolding over wine. You lot are detainments too — not fish and birds alone."

sentences.zh: 」及晉陽陷敗，與同志避周兵東北走。

translations.literal: " When Jinyang fell in defeat, he fled northeast with comrades to escape Zhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: " When Jinyang fell, he fled northeast with his comrades before the Zhou army.

sentences.zh: 山路險迥，懼有土賊，而晞溫酒服膏，曾不一廢。

translations.literal: The mountain road was dangerous and remote; they feared local bandits, yet Xi warmed his wine and applied salve without once discontinuing.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain road was treacherous and far; they feared bandits, yet Xi warmed his wine and took his salves without ever missing a day.

sentences.zh: 每未肯去，行侶尤之，曰：「莫尤我，我行事若不悔，久作三公矣。」

translations.literal: Time and again he would not consent to leave; his fellow travelers reproached him. He said, "Do not reproach me. Had my conduct been such that I did not regret it, I would long ago have been one of the Three Excellencies."
translations.idiomatic: Again and again he would not hurry on; his companions blamed him. He said, "Do not blame me. Had I not regretted my own ways, I would long since have been one of the Three Excellencies."
